brief: A school class bell that cannot ring: a small brass hand bell of a 1960s village school class, about 12 cm tall, polished warm brass with a few dull spots, a turned dark-brown wooden handle on its crown, standing and tilted towards the viewer so that its open mouth is visible: inside, the clapper (a small metal ball on a short rod) is wrapped in a little white cotton handkerchief with a thin blue border whose corner hangs out of the bell; a short torn end of an old thin dark leather loop dangles beside it.
